chapters.intro: Sunzi opens where every wise undertaking begins: not on the field but in the ancestral temple, counting. The chapter sets out five constants (the Way, Heaven, Earth, the commander and method) and seven questions that weigh one side against the other, then introduces two ideas that run through the whole book: 勢 shì, the momentum of a well-shaped situation, and 詭道 guǐ dào, the way of deception. Commentators from Cao Cao onwards read 計 jì as both plan and calculation: you think before you fight because the outcome is largely settled before the first step. For living, this is a chapter about deciding well: seeing clearly, weighing honestly, and never mistaking hope for a plan.
chapters.essence: Count before you commit; most victories are won at a table where no one is watching.
practices: Choose one decision you are facing and test it against the five constants: purpose, timing, ground, leadership and method. Write one honest sentence for each.
Ask the seven questions of yourself and of a rival or an alternative path, and mark every answer that was a hope rather than a fact.
Keep one plan quiet this week until it is ready; practise showing less than you have.

maxims.en: War is the gravest business of a state.
maxims.living: Recognise your great matters and give them unhurried thought.

maxims.en: Those who truly know them win.
maxims.living: To know a principle is to live it, not to recite it.

maxims.en: War is a way of illusion.
maxims.living: Do not show your hand before its time, and look twice at what others show you.

maxims.en: Strike where they are unready; go where they do not look.
maxims.living: The best opening is usually the one nobody else is watching.

maxims.en: Many counts win; few counts lose.
maxims.living: The side that has done the arithmetic usually prevails.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：兵者，國之大事，死生之地，存亡之道，不可不察也。
verses.en:
Master Sun said:
Arms are the gravest business of a state:
the ground on which men live or die,
the path by which a nation stands or falls.
Of this, nothing may be left unweighed.
verses.living: Some decisions are not like the others: a move abroad, a marriage, staking your savings on a business. Sunzi's first word is to recognise which matters carry this weight and to give them slow, deliberate attention rather than the quick reflex we give to email. Name your few great matters this year and refuse to decide them casually.

terms.gloss: arms, soldiers; by extension, warfare

verses.zh: 故經之以五事，校之以計，而索其情：一曰道，二曰天，三曰地，四曰將、五曰法。
verses.living: Before a launch or a negotiation, run it through a fixed checklist rather than through your mood that morning. The same five questions, asked the same way each time, expose what enthusiasm hides. A framework is not bureaucracy; it is a mirror that refuses to flatter.

terms.gloss: reckoning: plans and the calculation behind them
the Way: the shared purpose that binds people to those who lead them

verses.zh: 道者，令民與上同意者也，故可與之死，可與之生，民不畏危也。
verses.en:
The Way is what makes the people
of one mind with those above,
so that they will die with them,
live with them,
and not flinch at danger.
verses.living: A team that shares the purpose will carry a project through a bad quarter; a team that merely obeys will scatter at the first storm. Before asking anyone, a colleague or a teenager, to endure hardship alongside you, ask whether they truly share the why. Spend more time on alignment than on instruction.

verses.zh: 天者，陰陽、寒暑、時制也。地者，遠近、險易、廣狹、死生也。
verses.en:
Heaven is yin and yang,
cold and heat,
the measure of the seasons.
Earth is far and near,
rugged and easy,
open and narrow,
ground of death and ground of life.
verses.living: Every plan sits inside conditions you did not choose: the season of the market, the energy of your year, the terrain of your industry or your family. Timing and ground are not excuses but facts to be read. Ask of any venture: is this the season, and is this the place to stand?

terms.gloss: Heaven: timing, climate, the conditions of the moment
Earth: terrain, distance, position

verses.zh: 將者，智、信、仁、勇、嚴也。法者，曲制、官道、主用也。
verses.en:
The commander is wisdom and good faith,
humanity, courage and strictness.
Method is the ordering of units,
the duties of officers,
the governing of supply.
verses.living: Notice that humanity and strictness sit side by side in Sunzi's list. A parent or manager who is kind but never firm, or firm but never kind, holds only half the set. And method, who does what and where the money goes, is not dull detail; it is where good intentions turn into results.

terms.gloss: the commander, the one who leads in the field
method: organisation, rules, logistics

verses.zh: 凡此五者，將莫不聞，知之者勝，不知者不勝。
verses.living: Most of us have heard the basics: sleep, save, prepare, listen. The gap lies between having heard and knowing, between reciting a principle and living by it. Pick one rule you could lecture on and check honestly whether your week reflects it.

verses.zh: 故校之以計，而索其情，曰：主孰有道？將孰有能？天地孰得？法令孰行？兵衆孰強？士卒孰練？賞罰孰明？吾以此知勝負矣。
verses.en:
So compare them by reckoning
and search out how things truly stand. Ask:
Which ruler has the Way?
Which commander has the ability?
Who holds the advantages of Heaven and Earth?
Whose laws and orders are carried out?
Whose forces are stronger?
Whose soldiers are better trained?
Whose rewards and punishments are clear?
By these I know who will win and who will lose.
verses.living: Seven plain questions, asked of both sides, will tell you more than hope can. Before applying for a role or bidding for a contract, answer them for yourself and for the competition: who is better led, better prepared, more disciplined, clearer about what they reward. If the answers trouble you, you have learned something cheaply.

verses.zh: 將聽吾計，用之必勝，留之；將不聽吾計，用之必敗，去之。計利以聽，乃爲之勢，以佐其外。勢者，因利而制權也。
verses.en:
A commander who heeds my reckoning,
employed, will surely win: keep him.
A commander who ignores my reckoning,
employed, will surely lose: send him away.
Once the reckoning favours us and is heeded,
build shi, momentum,
to carry it beyond the plan.
Shi is this:
moving with what is advantageous,
you take hold of the scales.
verses.living: Planning at the desk is half the work; the other half is acting on a shifting balance once you are out in the world. Keep near you people who actually listen, and once the plan is sound, stop deliberating and build momentum. Then stay alert: momentum means adjusting to advantage as it appears, not clinging to the script.

terms.gloss: momentum, configuration: the stored force of a well-shaped position
the scales: adaptive judgement, leverage

verses.zh: 兵者，詭道也。故能而示之不能，用而示之不用，近而示之遠，遠而示之近；
verses.living: Read as wisdom rather than trickery, this is about not showing your hand too early. A writer need not announce the novel before it exists; a job-seeker need not reveal every option at the first interview. Learn too to see through others' displays: the buyer who seems indifferent may be the most eager.

terms.gloss: the way of deception: surprise, concealment, the unexpected

verses.zh: 利而誘之，亂而取之，實而備之，強而避之，怒而撓之，卑而驕之，逸而勞之，親而離之。
verses.living: Turn this list around and use it as a mirror: each line names a weakness by which you yourself can be moved. Greed, disorder, temper, vanity, fatigue and a rift with a friend are exactly the handles a pushy salesperson or a rival reaches for. Know which handle you carry most visibly, and keep it out of reach.

verses.zh: 攻其無備，出其不意。此兵家之勝，不可先傳也。
verses.en:
Strike where they are unready;
emerge where they do not look.
These are the strategist's victories,
and they cannot be told beforehand.
verses.living: The opening you need often lies where no one is looking: the neglected market, the unfashionable skill, the quiet hour before others wake. Such chances cannot be scripted from afar; they are seen only on the ground, in the moment. Prepare thoroughly, then trust yourself to improvise.

verses.zh: 夫未戰而廟算勝者，得算多也；未戰而廟算不勝者，得算少也。多算勝，少算不勝，而況於無算乎？吾以此觀之，勝負見矣。
verses.en:
Whoever wins the temple reckoning before battle
has more counting rods on his side;
whoever loses the temple reckoning before battle
has fewer.
More counts win, fewer counts lose,
and how much worse to have no count at all!
Looking at it this way,
I can see who will win and who will lose.
verses.living: Outcomes are usually settled at the kitchen table before they show in the world: in the budget, the training plan, the rehearsal. The worst position is not a poor calculation but none at all. Before any important move, sit down and count on paper what is for you and what is against.

terms.gloss: temple reckoning: the counting done in the ancestral hall before war

chapters.intro: The second chapter turns from calculation to cost. Sunzi itemises a campaign down to the glue and lacquer, and concludes that duration is the great enemy: long wars drain the state, invite opportunists and leave even the wise unable to repair the damage. Two memorable ideas emerge: 拙速 zhuō sù, 'clumsy speed', preferred to clever delay, and the practice of feeding on the enemy, living off what the field provides. Du Mu and Zhang Yu read the chapter as a treatise on economy rather than ferocity. For living, it is a lesson in burn rates, compounding costs and the discipline of finishing.
chapters.essence: Prize the result, not the struggle; nothing long drawn out has ever made anyone rich.
practices: Write down the true daily cost of one ongoing project or conflict, counting time, money, sleep and goodwill.
Finish one thing this week roughly and quickly instead of polishing it further.
Find one resource the situation already offers, such as feedback, a free tool or a rival's lesson, and use it instead of building from scratch.

maxims.en: Prize victory, not duration.
maxims.living: Measure effort by outcomes, not by how long you have endured.

maxims.en: We have heard of clumsy haste in war.
maxims.living: Rough and soon beats perfect and never.

maxims.en: One measure of their grain is worth twenty of ours.
maxims.living: Use what the field provides before hauling from home.

maxims.en: Defeat the enemy and grow stronger.
maxims.living: Win in a way that leaves you, and those you take in, stronger than before.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：凡用兵之法，馳車千駟，革車千乘，帶甲十萬，千里饋糧，則內外之費，賓客之用，膠漆之材，車甲之奉，日費千金，然後十萬之師舉矣。
verses.en:
Master Sun said:
In all the business of arms,
with a thousand swift chariots,
a thousand leather-armoured wagons,
a hundred thousand in mail,
and grain hauled a thousand li,
the costs at home and in the field,
the keep of envoys and guests,
glue and lacquer for repairs,
the upkeep of chariots and armour,
come to a thousand pieces of gold a day.
Only then can a hundred thousand take the field.
verses.living: Every serious undertaking has a daily burn rate, whether it is a start-up, a renovation or a lawsuit. Sunzi lists even the glue and lacquer: the small costs that quietly add up. Before you begin, write the real daily cost of the project, including what nobody budgets for, such as time, attention and goodwill.

terms.gloss: a Chinese mile, roughly half a kilometre

verses.zh: 其用戰也勝，久則鈍兵挫銳，攻城則力屈，久暴師則國用不足。夫鈍兵挫銳，屈力殫貨，則諸侯乘其弊而起，雖有智者，不能善其後矣。
verses.en:
When you fight, seek victory.
Drag it out, and weapons dull, edges blunt;
besiege a city, and your strength is spent;
keep the army long in the field,
and the state's resources fall short.
When weapons are dull and edges blunt,
strength drained and treasure gone,
neighbouring lords rise to profit from your exhaustion,
and even the wisest
cannot then mend what follows.
verses.living: Long fights wear down even the side that is right: a dispute with a neighbour, a project that never ships, a feud with a sibling. While you are spent, others take their chance. Decide early what a reasonable ending looks like, and close the matter before it closes you.

verses.zh: 故兵聞拙速，未睹巧之久也。夫兵久而國利者，未之有也。故不盡知用兵之害者，則不能盡知用兵之利也。
verses.en:
So we have heard of clumsy haste in war,
but never seen cleverness that lingers.
No state has ever profited from a long war.
Whoever does not fully grasp the harm of arms
cannot fully grasp their use.
verses.living: Done roughly and soon often beats done perfectly and late: ship the first version, send the imperfect apology, make the call today. Endless polishing is its own kind of defeat. And understand the downside of any tool, whether credit, conflict or ambition, before you trust yourself with its upside.

terms.gloss: clumsy speed: rough but swift action

verses.zh: 善用兵者，役不再籍，糧不三載，取用於國，因糧於敵，故軍食可足也。
verses.en:
One skilled in arms
does not levy troops a second time
nor ship provisions a third.
Bring your equipment from home,
forage your grain from the enemy,
and the army will have enough to eat.
verses.living: Raise resources once, then make the work feed itself: a side business that funds its own growth, a habit that rewards itself. Repeated appeals for more money, more time and more patience are a sign the design is wrong. Ask how the venture can supply what it consumes.

verses.zh: 國之貧於師者遠輸，遠輸則百姓貧；近師者貴賣，貴賣則百姓財竭，財竭則急於丘役。
verses.living: Costs compound: a long commute drains money and then energy, and the drained energy makes everything else dearer. Find the chain in your own life where one strain feeds the next, and break it at the first link. Moving closer to work, clearing one debt or dropping one draining commitment can lift several burdens at once.

verses.zh: 力屈財殫，中原內虛於家，百姓之費，十去其七；公家之費，破軍罷馬，甲冑矢弩，戟楯蔽櫓，丘牛大車，十去其六。
verses.en:
Strength spent, wealth exhausted,
households in the heartland stand empty.
Of the people's means,
seven parts in ten are gone.
Of the state's,
broken chariots, worn-out horses,
helmets, armour, arrows and crossbows,
halberds, shields and great mantlets,
oxen and heavy wagons,
six parts in ten are gone.
verses.living: Sunzi does the arithmetic of exhaustion: most of the cost of a long struggle is invisible at the start. Before entering a drawn-out conflict at work or in the family, picture the inventory afterwards: what friendships, health and savings will be left standing? If the answer is four parts in ten, look for another way.

verses.zh: 故智將務食於敵，食敵一鍾，當吾二十鍾；萁稈一石，當吾二十石。
verses.en:
So the wise commander takes pains to feed on the enemy.
One measure of their grain
is worth twenty of ours;
one bale of their fodder
worth twenty of our own.
verses.living: Use what the situation already provides rather than carrying everything from home. A competitor's public mistakes are free lessons; a critic's objection is raw material for your next draft. Knowledge gathered in the field is worth twenty times what you haul in from theory.

terms.gloss: a large measure of grain

verses.zh: 故殺敵者，怒也；取敵之利者，貨也。車戰得車十乘以上，賞其先得者，而更其旌旗，車雜而乘之，卒善而養之，是謂勝敵而益強。
verses.en:
What drives men to kill the foe is anger;
what draws them to seize his goods is reward.
In chariot fighting, when ten or more chariots are taken,
reward the first to capture one,
change the banners,
mix the captured chariots among our own,
treat the captured soldiers well and keep them.
This is called defeating the enemy and growing stronger.
verses.living: People need both a fire and a share: a reason to care and a part in what is won. Reward the first person who takes a risk, and when newcomers join from a rival firm or another school, make them truly yours: new colours, a real welcome, good treatment. A victory that honours the former opponent makes you stronger; one that humiliates breeds new enemies.

verses.zh: 故兵貴勝，不貴久。故知兵之將，生民之司命，國家安危之主也。
verses.en:
So in war, prize victory,
not duration.
The commander who understands war
holds the people's fate in his hands;
on him rests the safety or the peril of the state.
verses.living: Value the result, not the hours spent or the length of the struggle. Whoever leads, a parent, a manager, a founder, carries others' fortunes and should feel that weight as a reason to finish things well and swiftly. Long effort is not a virtue in itself; a good outcome is.

terms.gloss: arbiter of fate; the name of a star deity

chapters.intro: Chapter three, 謀攻 móu gōng, 'attacking by stratagem', holds Sunzi's most humane idea: the best victory leaves things whole. Taking the enemy's state and army intact (全 quán) ranks above breaking them, and the highest skill is to make an opponent yield without battle. The chapter ranks targets from plans to alliances to armies to walled cities, warns against rulers who meddle in what they do not understand, and closes with the famous counsel on knowing the other and knowing oneself. Commentators such as Mei Yaochen read it as the triumph of mind over force. For living, it teaches how to settle conflicts early, at the level of intention, and to win without wreckage.
chapters.essence: Win the thing whole: the finest fight is the one you made unnecessary.
practices: Take one current disagreement and ask what outcome would leave both the issue and the relationship intact; then propose it.
Before your next difficult conversation, write one paragraph on what you want and one on what the other person most fears or needs.
Notice one surge of anger this week that urges you to storm the wall, and postpone that action for a full day.

maxims.en: Bring them to yield without a fight.
maxims.living: The finest resolution makes the conflict unnecessary.

maxims.en: The highest warfare strikes at plans.
maxims.living: Meet a problem at the level of intention, before it hardens into position.

maxims.en: Where high and low want the same, they win.
maxims.living: Shared purpose outweighs superior resources.

maxims.en: The ready, awaiting the unready, win.
maxims.living: Preparation is a quiet advantage that compounds.

maxims.en: Know them, know yourself: a hundred battles, no peril.
maxims.living: Study the other side as carefully as you study yourself.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：夫用兵之法，全國爲上，破國次之，全軍爲上，破軍次之；全旅爲上，破旅次之；全卒爲上，破卒次之；全伍爲上，破伍次之。
verses.living: In a dispute, the best outcome usually leaves the other side, and the relationship, intact. Win a negotiation by breaking a supplier, or an argument by crushing a partner, and you own the ruins. From the largest matter to the smallest, aim to win the thing whole.

terms.gloss: whole, intact, complete

verses.zh: 是故百戰百勝，非善之善者也；不戰而屈人之兵，善之善者也。
verses.en:
So a hundred victories in a hundred battles
is not the summit of skill.
To bend the enemy's army without a battle:
that is the summit of skill.
verses.living: The best manager settles the conflict before it becomes a meeting; the best parent shapes the evening so the tantrum never comes. Winning every argument is a sign you are having too many arguments. Seek the arrangement that makes the fight unnecessary.

verses.zh: 故上兵伐謀，其次伐交，其次伐兵，其下攻城。攻城之法爲不得已。
verses.living: When something stands in your way, meet it at the earliest level: first the intention, then the relationships, then the conduct, and only last the entrenched position. If a colleague is set on a poor plan, engage the thinking behind it long before you are reduced to fighting a finished decision. Frontal assaults on fortified positions are where most energy is wasted.

terms.gloss: plans, strategy, counsel
alliances, connections

verses.zh: 修櫓轒轀，具器械，三月而後成，距堙，又三月而後已。將不勝其忿而蟻附之，殺士卒三分之一而城不拔者，此攻之災也。
verses.en:
Building shields and siege carts
and readying engines takes three months;
heaping the earthen ramps
takes three months more.
If the commander, unable to master his anger,
sends his men swarming up the walls like ants,
a third of them are killed
and still the city stands.
This is the calamity of siege.
verses.living: Anger makes us storm walls: the furious email, the all-out confrontation, the doubling down on a failing bet. The usual price is a third of your strength and nothing to show for it. When you feel the urge to swarm the wall, put the decision off until the heat has passed.

verses.zh: 故善用兵者，屈人之兵而非戰也，拔人之城而非攻也，毀人之國而非久也，必以全爭於天下。故兵不頓而利可全，此謀攻之法也。
verses.en:
So one skilled in arms
bends armies without battle,
takes cities without siege,
brings down states without long campaigns.
He contends for all under heaven by keeping things whole,
so his troops are not worn down
and the gain is complete.
This is the method of attacking by stratagem.
verses.living: Look for the route that wins without spending you: an offer so good the rival becomes a partner, a habit so easy it needs no willpower. The aim is gain without wreckage, so that your energy and your relationships are still there tomorrow. Before any campaign, ask whether a whole victory is available.

verses.zh: 故用兵之法，十則圍之，五則攻之，倍則分之，敵則能戰之，少則能逃之，不若則能避之。故小敵之堅，大敵之擒也。
verses.living: Match your approach to your real strength. A small firm that fights the giant head-on is simply swallowed; one that slips into a niche survives. In a household budget or a career, know when your position lets you push, when it calls for patience, and when it is wise to step aside without shame.

verses.zh: 夫將者，國之輔也。輔周，則國必強；輔隙，則國必弱。
verses.living: The people nearest the centre of any enterprise, a deputy, a co-founder, a spouse, are its frame. Where trust between them is tight, the whole holds; where there are gaps, everything rattles. Tend that closeness deliberately.

terms.gloss: support, bracing; the side-boards of a cart

verses.zh: 故君之所以患于軍者三：不知軍之不可以進而謂之進，不知軍之不可以退而謂之退，是謂“縻軍”；
verses.en:
A ruler can bring harm on his army in three ways.
Not knowing the army cannot advance,
he orders it forward;
not knowing the army cannot retreat,
he orders it back.
This is called hobbling the army.
verses.living: Leaders who are far from the work yet insist on steering it make the most expensive mistakes. If you manage people, ask before you order: can this actually move right now? If you are managed this way, bring the ground truth to the person deciding, clearly and early.

verses.zh: 不知三軍之事，而同三軍之政者，則軍士惑矣；不知三軍之權，而同三軍之任，則軍士疑矣。三軍既惑且疑，則諸侯之難至矣，是謂“亂軍引勝”。
verses.en:
Not knowing the army's affairs,
yet meddling in its administration,
he leaves the officers bewildered.
Not knowing the army's weighing of circumstance,
yet meddling in its command,
he leaves the officers in doubt.
Once the army is bewildered and in doubt,
trouble from the neighbouring lords arrives.
This is called unsettling your own army
and handing away the victory.
verses.living: Two voices giving orders breed confusion; authority without understanding breeds doubt. Parents who overrule each other in front of the children create exactly this. Decide who holds which responsibility, then let them hold it.

terms.gloss: discretion: weighing circumstances and adapting

verses.zh: 故知勝有五：知可以戰與不可以戰者勝，識衆寡之用者勝，上下同欲者勝，以虞待不虞者勝，將能而君不御者勝。此五者，知勝之道也。
verses.en:
So there are five ways to foreknow victory.
Who knows when to fight and when not to fight will win.
Who knows how to use both large and small forces will win.
Where high and low want the same, they will win.
Who waits, prepared, for the unprepared will win.
Whose commander is able and not reined in by the ruler will win.
These five are the way to foreknow victory.
verses.living: Read this as a checklist for any shared effort, a house move, a product launch, a family holiday: is this the right fight; can we work at the right scale; do we all want the same thing; are we readier than the problem; does the person in charge have room to act? Five honest yeses predict success better than talent does.

terms.gloss: forethought, readiness

verses.zh: 故曰：知彼知己者，百戰不殆；不知彼而知己，一勝一負，不知彼，不知己，每戰必殆。
verses.en:
So it is said:
know them, know yourself,
and a hundred battles bring no peril.
Know yourself but not them,
and you win one, lose one.
Know neither them nor yourself,
and every battle is mortal danger.
verses.living: Most failures come from seeing only half the picture. In a hard conversation, know your own triggers and also what the other person fears; in a career move, know your strengths and also what the employer truly needs. Self-knowledge alone gives even odds; add understanding of the other, and you are seldom in danger.

terms.gloss: peril, danger

chapters.intro: This chapter turns on 形 xíng, the visible form or disposition of a force: how it stands before anything moves. Sunzi's claim is quietly radical: victory is decided by preparation long before the clash, so the skilled commander first makes himself unbeatable and then waits for the enemy to offer an opening. The commentators stress that defence is a matter of self-mastery, while the opportunity to win lies with the other side and cannot be forced. The chapter ends with a chain of measurement, from ground to quantity to number to weighing to victory, and the image of dammed water released down a gorge: form so well prepared that its release looks effortless.
chapters.essence: Make yourself unbeatable first; then the right moment will find you ready.
practices: List the three things that could sink your most important project this month and close one of them before you start anything new.
Before your next big decision, write down the numbers: time, money, energy, people. Weigh them honestly on one page.
Spend one day doing the quiet, unglamorous work that no one will praise but that makes failure less likely.

maxims.zh: 先爲不可勝，以待敵之可勝
maxims.en: First become unbeatable, then wait for the moment they can be beaten.
maxims.living: Secure your own position before you chase an opportunity.

maxims.en: Victory can be foreseen; it cannot be forced.
maxims.living: Prepare fully, then let the opening arrive instead of grabbing at it.

maxims.en: No name for cleverness, no credit for courage.
maxims.living: The best work often looks easy, and that is the proof of its quality.

maxims.en: The winning army wins first, then seeks the battle.
maxims.living: Do the winning in preparation, so the event itself is only confirmation.

maxims.en: Stand on ground where you cannot lose.
maxims.living: Choose positions you can hold before choosing positions that dazzle.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：昔之善戰者，先爲不可勝，以待敵之可勝。不可勝在己，可勝在敵。故善戰者，能爲不可勝，不能使敵之必可勝。故曰：勝可知，而不可爲。
verses.en:
Master Sun said:
those of old who were good at war
first made themselves unbeatable,
then waited for the enemy to become beatable.

Being unbeatable rests with us;
being beatable rests with them.
So the skilled can make themselves unconquerable,
but cannot make the enemy sure to fall.

Hence the saying:
victory can be known,
it cannot be made.
verses.living: Your part is to remove your own weaknesses; whether a chance appears is partly up to the world. Before a job interview, a launch or a hard conversation, put your energy into what you control: preparation, rest, clarity. Then watch for the opening without trying to manufacture it.

terms.gloss: unbeatable, a position that cannot be overcome

verses.zh: 不可勝者，守也；可勝者，攻也。守則不足，攻則有餘。善守者，藏於九地之下，善攻者，動於九天之上，故能自保而全勝也。
verses.living: When resources are thin, guard and consolidate; when they overflow, go forward. A small business in a lean year should protect cash and customers, not open a second shop. Know which season you are in, and commit fully to the posture it calls for, whether that is lying low or moving boldly.

terms.gloss: the ninefold earth, the deepest concealment
the ninefold heaven, the highest, swiftest movement

verses.zh: 見勝不過衆人之所知，非善之善者也；戰勝而天下曰善，非善之善者也。故舉秋毫不爲多力，見日月不爲明目，聞雷霆不爲聰耳。
verses.en:
To see a victory only when everyone can see it
is not the best of the best.
To win in battle and have the whole world cry 'well done'
is not the best of the best.

Lifting an autumn hair is no sign of strength;
seeing sun and moon, no sign of sharp eyes;
hearing thunder, no sign of keen ears.
verses.living: Real foresight notices what others have not yet noticed: the early sign of burnout in a colleague, the small cost that will compound. Applause is a poor measure of skill. The deepest competence often goes unseen because it dealt with the problem before it became visible.

verses.zh: 古之所謂善戰者，勝於易勝者也。故善戰者之勝也，無智名，無勇功。故其戰勝不忒，不忒者，其所措必勝，勝已敗者也。
verses.en:
Those the ancients called skilled in war
won where winning was easy.
So their victories brought
no fame for wisdom,
no merit for courage.

Their battles were won without error;
without error, because all they set in place
was bound to win:
they conquered those already defeated.
verses.living: Arrange things so that the decisive moment is easy. A writer who drafts a little every morning finishes the book without heroics; a household that automates savings never needs willpower at the end of the month. If success looks dull from outside, you probably built it well.

terms.gloss: without deviation or error

verses.zh: 故善戰者，立於不敗之地，而不失敵之敗也。是故勝兵先勝而後求戰，敗兵先戰而後求勝。善用兵者，修道而保法，故能爲勝敗之政。
verses.en:
So the skilled take their stand on ground where they cannot lose,
and do not miss the moment the enemy can.

The victorious army wins first, then seeks battle;
the defeated army fights first, then looks for a way to win.

The one who uses troops well
cultivates the Way and keeps to method,
and so holds in hand
the government of victory and defeat.
verses.living: Before you pitch the client, ask for the raise or enter the negotiation, the outcome should already be largely settled by your research, your alternatives and your relationships. People who walk in hoping to improvise a win usually lose. Tend the basics, your values and your systems, and results begin to answer to you.

terms.gloss: the Way; here the moral and practical coherence that binds people to their leader
method, law, organisation

verses.zh: 兵法：一曰度，二曰量，三曰數，四曰稱，五曰勝。地生度，度生量，量生數，數生稱，稱生勝。
verses.living: Good decisions run on a chain of honest measurement. Thinking of moving city for work? Measure the ground (costs, commute, family), estimate what you need, count what you have, weigh the two side by side. Victory is the last link, never the first.

terms.gloss: measurement of ground and distance
weighing, comparing one side against the other

verses.zh: 故勝兵若以鎰稱銖，敗兵若以銖稱鎰。勝者之戰民也，若決積水於千仞之溪者，形也。
verses.en:
So a winning army is like a heavy weight set against a grain;
a losing army, like a grain set against a weight.

When the victor sends his people into battle
it is like bursting a dam of gathered water
into a gorge a thousand fathoms deep:
this is form.
verses.living: Accumulate quietly until the balance is overwhelming, then release all at once. A musician who has practised a piece for months plays it with ease on the night; a team that has rehearsed a launch lets it go like water through a gate. The force was stored long before it was seen.

terms.gloss: form, disposition; strength gathered and shaped before it moves
a heavy weight and a tiny one, roughly five hundred to one

chapters.intro: Where the previous chapter dealt with 形 xíng, static form, this one turns to 勢 shì: the dynamic potential that arrangement creates, like a boulder poised at the top of a slope or a crossbow fully drawn. Sunzi introduces the pairing 奇正 qí zhèng, the orthodox move that engages and the unexpected one that wins, and shows how their combinations are endless, like the five notes, colours and tastes. Commentators such as Cao Cao and Li Quan read 勢 as leverage: a commander who sets up the right configuration does not need to demand heroism from individuals. For a reader today, this is the chapter on systems, timing and creative recombination.
chapters.essence: Do not push the stone; place it on the slope.
practices: Identify one goal you are forcing through willpower and redesign the setting so it happens almost by itself.
Take a routine task and add one unexpected element: a different order, a new format, a surprise for the person receiving it.
Notice a moment this week when you need to act quickly, and when it comes, act in one short, decisive motion.

maxims.en: Engage with the orthodox; win with the unexpected.
maxims.living: Meet people on expected ground, then bring the fresh element that decides it.

maxims.zh: 奇正相生，如循環之無端
maxims.en: Surprise and the expected give birth to each other, a ring without an end.
maxims.living: Creativity is endless recombination of a few plain elements.

maxims.en: Their force is steep; their timing, short.
maxims.living: Build up pressure patiently, then act in one quick stroke.

maxims.en: Seek it in configuration; do not demand it of people.
maxims.living: Fix the situation before you blame the person.

maxims.en: Like rolling a round stone down a mountain a thousand fathoms high.
maxims.living: Good positioning makes action feel effortless.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：凡治衆如治寡，分數是也；鬥衆如鬥寡，形名是也；三軍之衆，可使必受敵而無敗者，奇正是也；兵之所加，如以碫投卵者，虛實是也。
verses.en:
Master Sun said:
to govern many as you govern few
is a matter of division and number;
to fight with many as you fight with few
is a matter of signals, form and name.

That the whole host may take the enemy's blow
and never be broken:
this is the unexpected and the orthodox.
That an army falls on its target
like a whetstone thrown at an egg:
this is empty and full.
verses.living: Growth is manageable only with structure. A team of fifty can move like a team of five if roles are divided clearly and signals are simple. Before you expand, a family budget, a club or a company, decide how it will be split and how people will know what to do.

terms.gloss: division and numbering: organising units
forms and names: flags, drums and signals
the unexpected and the orthodox

verses.zh: 凡戰者，以正合，以奇勝。故善出奇者，無窮如天地，不竭如江海。終而復始，日月是也。死而更生，四時是也。
verses.en:
In all battle,
join with the orthodox,
win with the unexpected.

One who is good at the unexpected
is boundless as heaven and earth,
unending as rivers and seas;
ending and beginning again,
like sun and moon;
dying and coming back to life,
like the four seasons.
verses.living: Show up with the solid, expected work, then let the original touch decide the matter. In a job application, the competent CV gets you into the room; the one unusual project or question is what people remember. Keep a store of fresh ideas that renews itself, like seasons, by reading and wandering widely.

terms.gloss: the orthodox, direct, expected force
the unexpected, indirect, surprising force

verses.zh: 聲不過五，五聲之變，不可勝聽也；色不過五，五色之變，不可勝觀也；味不過五，五味之變，不可勝嘗也；戰勢不過奇正，奇正之變，不可勝窮也。奇正相生，如循環之無端，孰能窮之哉！
verses.en:
There are no more than five notes,
yet their changes are more than ear can hear.
There are no more than five colours,
yet their changes are more than eye can see.
There are no more than five tastes,
yet their changes are more than tongue can know.

In battle there are only two forces, surprise and the expected,
yet their changes are more than mind can exhaust.
Each gives birth to the other,
a ring that has no end.
Who could ever exhaust them?
verses.living: You do not need endless resources to be inventive; a few elements in fresh combinations are enough. A cook with five ingredients, a designer with three colours, a parent with a handful of games can keep things new for years. When you feel stuck, recombine what you have rather than waiting for something new.

verses.zh: 激水之疾，至於漂石者，勢也；鷙鳥之疾，至於毀折者，節也。故善戰者，其勢險，其節短。勢如擴弩，節如發機。
verses.en:
The rush of a torrent
that sweeps away boulders:
that is force.
The swoop of a hawk
that breaks its prey:
that is timing.

So the skilled in war
make their force steep
and their timing short.
Force is the crossbow drawn full;
timing, the release of the trigger.
verses.living: Power has two parts: the pressure you build and the instant you let it go. A salesperson builds trust over weeks, then makes the request in one clear sentence. Do not dribble your energy out in half measures; gather it, then strike once and cleanly.

terms.gloss: momentum, the force that comes from configuration
timing, the measured interval of the strike

verses.zh: 紛紛紜紜，鬥亂而不可亂；渾渾沌沌，形圓而不可敗。亂生於治，怯生於勇，弱生於強。治亂，數也；勇怯，勢也；強弱，形也。
verses.living: What looks messy from outside, a busy kitchen, a household with young children, a startup in launch week, can be deeply ordered inside. Equally, apparent weakness can be a deliberate posture. Courage is rarely a fixed trait; it rises and falls with the situation, so arrange situations that make bravery easier for yourself and others.

verses.zh: 故善動敵者，形之，敵必從之；予之，敵必取之。以利動之，以卒待之。
verses.living: People respond to what they are shown and offered. Read this as a lesson in seeing through others' bait: the free trial, the flattering offer, the 'limited time' deal. And in your own work, lead with genuine benefit, then be ready when people come towards it.

verses.zh: 故善戰者，求之於勢，不責於人，故能擇人而任勢。任勢者，其戰人也，如轉木石。木石之性，安則靜，危則動，方則止，圓則行。
verses.en:
So the skilled in war
seek it in the force of configuration
and do not lay the burden on people;
they can choose their people
and trust to the configuration.

One who trusts to configuration
sends people into battle
like rolling logs and stones.
It is the nature of logs and stones
to rest on level ground and move on a slope,
to stop when square
and roll when round.
verses.living: When results disappoint, look first at the setup, not at the person. A child who will not do homework may need a quiet table and a set hour, not a lecture; a team missing deadlines may need clearer priorities, not more pressure. Design the slope and people will roll.

terms.gloss: to rely on configuration rather than individual effort

verses.zh: 故善戰人之勢，如轉圓石於千仞之山者，勢也。
verses.en:
So the force of those who are skilled at war
is like a round stone rolled
down a mountain a thousand fathoms high:
that is shì.
verses.living: The hard work is getting the stone to the top and making it round; after that, a touch is enough. Spend most of your effort on position: skills, relationships, reputation. Then a single small push, an email, a proposal, a call, can carry enormous weight.

chapters.intro: 虛實 xū shí, 'empty and full', names the play of weakness and strength, absence and presence, that runs through every encounter. Sunzi teaches the commander to set the terms, to move others rather than be moved, and to strike where the opponent is thin while concealing his own shape until it becomes formless. The chapter's great image is water, which has no constant shape and wins by yielding to the ground. Commentators such as Du Mu and Zhang Yu saw this as the heart of the whole book: the art of meeting fullness with emptiness and emptiness with fullness. For living, it is a chapter about initiative, focus and adaptability.
chapters.essence: Be like water: set the terms, find the gaps, and never keep one shape for long.
practices: Arrive early to one important meeting or event this week and use the extra minutes to settle and observe.
Choose one goal and drop or delegate two smaller ones so your strength is concentrated, not spread thin.
When a plan meets resistance, change its shape instead of pushing harder: try another route, time or format.

maxims.en: Move others; do not be moved by them.
maxims.living: Set the agenda instead of reacting to everyone else's.

maxims.en: Strike where they do not guard.
maxims.living: Look for the unmet need, the neglected corner, the open door.

maxims.en: Guard everywhere, and you are thin everywhere.
maxims.living: Trying to cover everything leaves you weak at every point.

maxims.en: The shape of an army is like water.
maxims.living: Adapt to the ground in front of you rather than holding a fixed shape.

maxims.en: Water has no constant shape.
maxims.living: Flexibility is not weakness; it is how water cuts stone.

verses.zh: 孫子曰：凡先處戰地而待敵者佚，後處戰地而趨戰者勞，故善戰者，致人而不致於人。
verses.en:
Master Sun said:
whoever reaches the field first and waits for the enemy
is at ease;
whoever arrives late and hurries into battle
is worn out.

So the skilled in war
bring others to them
and are not brought.
verses.living: Being early is a strategy. Arrive before the meeting, start the project before the deadline looms, prepare before the talk with your teenager. When you have set the ground and the pace, you can meet others calmly while they hurry to catch up.

terms.gloss: to bring others to you, to hold the initiative

verses.zh: 能使敵人自至者，利之也；能使敵人不得至者，害之也，故敵佚能勞之，飽能飢之，安能動之。出其所不趨，趨其所不意。行千里而不勞者，行於無人之地也。
verses.living: People move towards benefit and away from cost; design your proposals with that in mind, honestly. And the easiest road is often through empty country: the niche nobody serves, the skill few bother to learn. A career built where competition is thin can travel very far without exhaustion.

verses.zh: 攻而必取者，攻其所不守也；守而必固者，守其所不攻也。故善攻者，敵不知其所守；善守者，敵不知其所攻。微乎微乎，至於無形。神乎神乎，至於無聲，故能爲敵之司命。
verses.en:
To take what you attack, attack what is not defended;
to hold what you defend, defend what will not be attacked.

So against the good attacker
the enemy does not know what to defend;
against the good defender
the enemy does not know what to attack.

Subtle, so subtle,
reaching formlessness;
mysterious, so mysterious,
reaching soundlessness.
So he becomes master of the enemy's fate.
verses.living: Do not announce every plan before it is ready. A founder who keeps the next product quiet, or a negotiator who does not reveal her walk-away point, keeps room to move. Discretion is not dishonesty; it is simply not handing others the map before the journey.

terms.gloss: formless, having no shape that can be read
master of fate, the arbiter of life and death

verses.zh: 進而不可御者，衝其虛也；退而不可追者，速而不可及也。故我欲戰，敵雖高壘深溝，不得不與我戰者，攻其所必救也；我不欲戰，雖畫地而守之，敵不得與我戰者，乖其所之也。
verses.en:
Advance and no one can resist, if you strike at the empty;
withdraw and no one can follow, if you are too swift to be caught.

So when I want battle,
though the enemy sits behind high walls and deep moats,
he must come out,
for I strike what he must save.

When I do not want battle,
though I hold only a line drawn on the ground,
he cannot engage me,
for I turn him aside from his course.
verses.living: Influence comes from touching what matters most to the other side. In a stalled negotiation, address the concern they cannot ignore, their deadline or their reputation, and they will come to the table. And when you wish to avoid a pointless quarrel, a light redirection often works better than a wall.

terms.gloss: empty, thin, unguarded

verses.zh: 故形人而我無形，則我專而敵分。我專爲一，敵分爲十，是以十攻其一也，則我衆而敵寡；能以衆擊寡者，則吾之所與戰者，約矣。吾所與戰之地不可知，不可知，則敵所備者多；敵所備者多，則吾之所與戰者，寡矣。
verses.en:
Make the enemy show his form while you remain formless,
and you are concentrated while he is divided.
I am one; he is split into ten.
Then it is ten against one,
and I am many where he is few.

If I can strike the few with the many,
those I fight are already in straits.

Where I will fight must not be known.
Unknown, the enemy must guard many places;
guarding many, those I meet at any one
are few.
verses.living: Concentration is the great multiplier. If you spread your week across ten goals you meet each one with a tenth of yourself; choose one and you bring all of it. A student revising one subject deeply each day outperforms one who skims everything at once.

terms.gloss: concentrated, unified
divided, dispersed

verses.zh: 故備前則後寡，備後則前寡，備左則右寡，備右則左寡，無所不備，則無所不寡。寡者，備人者也；衆者，使人備己者也。
verses.living: You cannot defend against every possible criticism, risk or rival. A product that tries to please every user pleases none deeply; a person who tries to avoid every disapproval ends up with no shape at all. Decide what you will leave unguarded, and put your strength where it counts.

verses.zh: 故知戰之地，知戰之日，則可千里而會戰。不知戰地，不知戰日，則左不能救右，右不能救左，前不能救後，後不能救前，而況遠者數十里，近者數里乎？
verses.en:
Know the place of battle,
know the day of battle,
and you may march a thousand miles to meet it.

Know neither the place nor the day,
and the left cannot help the right,
the right cannot help the left,
the front cannot help the rear,
the rear cannot help the front,

how much less when they lie tens of miles apart,
or even a few?
verses.living: Clear time and place turn scattered people into a coordinated force. A family reunion, a product launch or a group trip falls apart without a fixed date and venue. Name the when and the where early, and others can travel any distance to meet you there.

verses.zh: 以吾度之，越人之兵雖多，亦奚益於勝敗哉？故曰：勝可爲也。敵雖衆，可使無鬥。故策之而知得失之計，作之而知動靜之理，形之而知死生之地，角之而知有餘不足之處。
verses.living: Size alone does not decide outcomes; understanding does. Before you face a large competitor or a daunting exam, probe: try a small test, ask a question, run a pilot. Each light touch tells you where the strength is thick and where it runs thin.

terms.gloss: to test, to probe by a light clash

verses.zh: 故形兵之極，至於無形。無形，則深間不能窺，智者不能謀。因形而措勝於衆，衆不能知；人皆知我所以勝之形，而莫知吾所以制勝之形。故其戰勝不復，而應形於無窮。
verses.en:
So the height of giving an army form
is to reach formlessness.
Formless, the deepest spy cannot peer in,
the wisest cannot lay plans against you.

Victory is placed before the crowd according to form,
and the crowd cannot grasp it.
Everyone sees the shape by which I won;
no one sees the shape by which I shaped the win.

So no victory is repeated:
each answers form with form, without end.
verses.living: Others will copy what you did; they rarely see how you decided to do it. Rather than repeating last year's winning formula, keep the underlying way of thinking and let the outward form change. A teacher who reads each class freshly never runs out of lessons.

verses.zh: 夫兵形象水，水之形，避高而趨下，兵之形，避實而擊虛。水因地而制流，兵因敵而制勝。故兵無常勢，水無常形，能因敵變化而取勝者，謂之神。
verses.en:
An army's form is like water.
Water's form avoids the heights and runs to the low;
an army's form avoids the full and strikes the empty.

Water shapes its flow by the ground;
an army shapes its victory by the enemy.

So an army has no constant force,
water no constant shape.
One who can win by changing with the enemy
is called divine.
verses.living: Flow towards openings and around obstacles rather than through them. If a door at work is firmly closed, find the one that is ajar: another team, another format, another season. Rigidity breaks; responsiveness keeps moving, and over time it carves its own course.

terms.gloss: full, solid, strongly held
spirit, the uncanny, beyond ordinary understanding

verses.zh: 故五行無常勝，四時無常位，日有短長，月有死生。
verses.living: Nothing holds the upper hand for ever: not your rival, not your slump, not your winning streak. Hold good times lightly and hard times patiently. Change is the one constant, and it is the friend of anyone who keeps adapting.

terms.gloss: the five phases: wood, fire, earth, metal, water
